tables.title: Specified CoSQA replication comparison
notes: One frozen confirmatory comparison on capped CoSQA H. The displayed interval is the group-bootstrap 95% interval. Practical equivalence uses the frozen joint rule: both cluster-t and bootstrap 95% intervals strictly inside ±0.005, with the required changed-group count. The rule applies to this ENTR−RAND20 per-query best3 comparison.

tables.title: Endpoint contrasts under the same candidate pool
notes: Post hoc paired diagnostic. Single-candidate advantage is ENTR Top1 minus uniform single selection; best3 advantage uses ENTR best3 minus RAND20. Their direct difference changes both count and aggregation. Adjusted intervals apply to the four direct endpoint contrasts. This quantity is distinct from the exact-random B+G decomposition in S8.

tables.title: Fixed20 adoption with matched prediction heads
notes: CoSQA D: 1,490 queries, 512 groups. Fixed20 adopts the top 20% of eligible actions in each held-out fold, rounded down, including negative predictions. All heads share actions and folds. Intervals are 95% group-bootstrap intervals conditional on fitted out-of-fold (OOF) heads. Conditional feature increments retain the separate eight-comparison family in the source protocol; head-mean intervals shown here are not adjusted increment tests.

tables.title: Executable fusion and label-assisted candidate opportunity
notes: CoSQA D: 1,490 queries, 512 groups. Changes are relative to the original query. RRF3/RRF4 comparisons retain their four-comparison family; other displayed policies are descriptive. ENTR best3 needs relevance labels and is not executable. Fusion creates a new ranking, so candidate best3 is not its upper bound.

tables.title: Frozen full-H execution stages
notes: Full H: 8,530 queries, 1,963 groups. These predefined descriptive estimates are separate from the capped-H replication test. Retention is a proportion of nonnegative candidate gain with the original query available. CE pairs count incurred cross-encoder work, including work preceding fallback; they do not measure latency. RIDGE_verified also includes queries that were not actually verified and retain gain-stage predictions.

tables.title: Top1 and best3 under two T5 weights
notes: Each domain uses the same 512 matched historical queries/groups. Each weight retains its own complete candidate pool. Top1 and best3 changes use the original query as reference; ENTR−uniform uses a single-candidate random reference. Eight Top1/best3 effects form the original adjusted family. These used-sample sensitivity analyses are separate from the new 25,600-group confirmation in main Table II.

tables.title: Full-H opportunity-loss and verification accounting
notes: Each retriever uses all 8,530 queries in complete H, across 1,963 connected groups. Available gain is max(best3 ENTR RR@100 minus original-query RR@100, 0), retaining the original query as a safety option. For a stage change D and available gain U, unretained positive gain is U−max(D,0), and ranking loss is max(−D,0). The displayed means satisfy mean(U)−mean(D)=mean(unretained gain)+mean(ranking loss); Table S5 reports the corresponding net changes and positive-gain retention.

These are descriptive arithmetic summaries of the frozen outcomes, not a new comparison family or confidence interval. Verification pairs and input tokens are cumulative charged workload. Later risk fallback does not refund verification already performed. The verified-stage policy also includes queries not selected for cross-encoder scoring; their gain-stage predictions proceed to risk assessment.
Source: artifact/numerical/data/full_H_stages_CodeBERT.jsonl.gz and full_H_stages_BM25.jsonl.gz. Run tools/rebuild_s7.py --check to recompute all six rows.

tables.title: Candidate-count and aggregation decomposition
notes: Post hoc analysis, with 24 multiplicity-adjusted comparisons. AdvTest: 2,048 queries/594 groups; CoSQA D: 1,490/512. B=S(1,mean)−S(3,mean); G=S(3,mean)−S(3,best3). Positive B/G indicates a reduction in selector advantage. Direction requires both adjusted intervals on the same side of zero and sufficient nonzero groups. ENTR−PROB rows are direct component differences.

tables.title: StaQC confirmation and descriptive controls
notes: StaQC: 13,312 queries/groups and a 16,384-code corpus. The two CodeBERT ENTR B/G rows are the frozen confirmation family. All PROB/BM25 and direct-selector controls remain prespecified descriptive comparisons with ordinary 95% intervals. “Descriptive” is a role, not a directional decision. The design was locally sealed, not externally preregistered.

tables.title: UniXcoder and paired retriever contrasts
notes: Twelve adjusted comparisons on previously used CoSQA D and StaQC samples. UX=UniXcoder; CB=CodeBERT. Paired differences subtract the named retriever component using the same query outcomes and retain dependence. Unresolved direct differences do not establish retriever equivalence.

tables.title: Matched two-weight B/G sensitivity
notes: AdvTest and CoSQA each use 512 matched queries/groups, a fixed CodeBERT retriever, and each T5 weight's own pool. The 24-comparison family includes two domains, ENTR/PROB B/G and local/base/base-minus-local. Unresolved differences do not establish weight equivalence. Main Table II reports the separate six-comparison confirmation on 25,600 new groups.

tables.title: Agreement of the original human-review returns
notes: Unweighted agreement for the original returned judgments. Unknown relevance is a category in the nominal analysis; linear-weighted κ uses the jointly judged 0/1/2 subset with coverage reported. These results are separate from the supplemental 344-panel-per-reviewer agreement. Both reviewers' original labels remain unchanged.

notes: Each row is a query-level event marked by reviewer A, reviewer B, both on the same rewrite, or either reviewer. Rows can overlap. Estimates and conservative intervals concern the same finite H8530 frame as S13. The complete eight-stratum records remain in TABLES.json.

notes: Eight arms share 32,768 training rows and 1,024 updates. Each displayed contrast subtracts baseline L; own denotes the arm's own generated pool. S3 is ENTR best3 minus exact-random best3; Top1 gain is relative to the original query. The original family contains 28 comparisons. These finite-budget controls do not recover the full effects of historical 93,750-update training. Settings and the separate fixed-historical-pool view are documented in S21 and the source protocol.

Both reviewers gave informed consent before participating, after learning the study purpose and review tasks, and agreed to share de-identified annotations and rationales. The paper identifies reviewers as A/B and reports aggregate statistics; the reproduction materials retain anonymous item-level annotations and rationales without reviewer identities. No formal ethics review or exemption determination was sought for this study.
